title: Hurricane Simon Paralyzes Towns and Highways in Jalisco Amid Forecast That It Will Make Landfall
author: Juan Carlos G. Partida
content:
_This article by[Juan Carlos G.
Partida](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Juan%20Carlos%20G.%20Partida)
originally appeared in the [October 11, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/11/estados/hucaracan-
simon-paraliza-pueblos-y-carreteras-en-jalisco-ante-pronostico-de-que-toque-
tierra), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Punta Pérula, Jalisco**. This morning, with a still uncertain forecast of
where it will make landfall, if it does so in Jalisco, Category 4 Hurricane
Simon has the population of the entire coast of the state shut in, and
**mobility paralyzed in towns and on highways** , under a rain that has not
stopped since Saturday night, but which so far has not caused any casualties,
and only numerous floods are being reported.

In this locality of the municipality of La Huerta, a community of fishermen
and small tourist hotels located in the middle of the Jalisco coastline, since
Saturday night people have avoided going out due to the constant and heavy
rain that is beginning to flood various points.

After 10 in the morning, according to the National Water Commission, Simon is
50 kilometers offshore, which generates greater uncertainty among visitors and
residents given the possibility that the hurricane, which has shown **an
erratic trajectory** , will finally move toward land.

It does not seem that this will happen, but while the storm decides whether to
continue its trajectory parallel to the coast or to hurl itself against the
central Jalisco beaches as was announced on Saturday, gusts of wind shake palm
trees, raise **waves of up to 5 meters** , and force people to reinforce the
placement of boards to avoid any surprises.

Hundreds of Federal Electricity Commission workers in numerous crews cover
practically the entire coastal territory and fill hotels, stock up on supplies
at one of the few open businesses, or simply skip breakfast, while waiting to
learn what damage the storm will bring to the electrical grid, in an
unexpected boost to the area's economy.

The deployment of personnel from the Army, the National Guard, and both
national and state Civil Protection is also notable given the constant
patrols, although people in the most vulnerable areas were evacuated on
Saturday.

This Sunday morning, loudspeaker alerts could be heard announcing that "we are
on red alert" and urging people to remain sheltered and not travel.

![People sit on a seawall under cloudy skies on the Jalisco
coast](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/hurricane-
simon-jalisco-02.jpg)On Sunday morning, loudspeaker alerts announced that "we
are on red alert" and urged people to stay sheltered and not travel. Photo:
Arturo Campos Cedillo

Jalisco Civil Protection alone sent **200 rescuers** to the coast from its
inland bases, particularly from Guadalajara. That institution is expected
shortly to offer an update on the forecast and toll of the hurricane from its
regional headquarters in Puerto Vallarta.
